title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 2 of Grothendieck's May 1966 letter to Tate, the programme 'De Rham cohomology is a crystal'. Section 2.2 is stated under the optimistic assumption that no isogeny ('isogénisation') is needed.

(1) Setup. Crystals of modules on S are taken to form an abelian category. Its derived category is the category of 'complexes of crystals'. Such a complex K evaluates on each object (U -> T) of the crystalline site C of S, giving an object K_T of D(O_T). K is pseudo-coherent (or perfect, etc.) if every K_T is. In modern terms: a quasi-coherent derived crystal is a compatible system of K_T in D_qc(T) with base-change isomorphisms. Equivalently it is an object of D(O_{S/Z,cris}) whose cohomology sheaves are crystals, or (Bhatt–Lurie) a quasi-coherent complex on the de Rham / crystalline stack.

(2) Desired theory. To each smooth proper f: X -> S, attach an absolute complex of crystals DR(f) on S (crystalline site of S over Spec Z), called the crystalline de Rham cohomology of f. Required properties:
- DR(f) is perfect.
- Its formation commutes with arbitrary base change (derived pullback).
- It is contravariantly functorial in X/S.
- Künneth: DR(f x_S g) ≅ DR(f) ⊗^L DR(g).
- Duality: for relative dimension d, a perfect pairing DR(f) ⊗ DR(f) -> T^d[shift 2d], where T^d is the Tate crystal (corrected by hand to 'weight 2d').
- Comparison: the value on the trivial thickening, DR(f)(S), is isomorphic to Rf_*(Ω^•_{X/S}), compatibly with base change, Künneth and duality.
The non-proper case is deliberately set aside; it would be needed for a serious link with Washnitzer–Monsky.

(3) Section 2.3 begins. For each prime p, restrict to S_p = V(p·1) (derived restriction). By base change this is DR(f_p). The relative Frobenius X_p -> X_p^{(p/S_p)}, together with functoriality and base change, gives F_p: DR(f)_p^{(p)} -> DR(f)_p. The next page uses duality to define V with FV = VF = p^{2d}. So the isocrystal DR(f)⊗Q becomes a 'bi-isocrystal', i.e. an F-isocrystal at every prime simultaneously, on an S living over Z.

The purpose is to make the Gauss–Manin connection, the Leray/Katz–Oda spectral sequence and Frobenius structures all come from a single crystalline object. This is the programme realised (for S over a p-adic base, one prime at a time) by Berthelot 1974 and Berthelot–Ogus.
errors: Crystals of (quasi-coherent) modules do not form an abelian category in general. Cokernels are fine, but kernels fail to satisfy the crystal condition because the transition maps u*M_T -> M_{T'} need flatness. So 'the derived category of the abelian category of crystals' is not well defined as stated. Modern treatments use complexes in D(O_{S/cris}) with crystal cohomology, a homotopy limit of the D(T), or quasi-coherent sheaves on the crystalline/de Rham stack.

The duality target: in cohomological indexing the pairing DR(f) ⊗^L DR(f) -> T^d should land in T^d[-2d], since the trace lives in degree 2d. Grothendieck's '[2d]' with the gloss 'translate degrees by 2d' is a sign-convention ambiguity. 'x' should also be derived tensor.

The weight of the Tate crystal was hand-corrected from d to 2d. With Frobenius acting by p^d on the top class, this matches 'weight 2d' in his bi-crystal conventions. The resulting relation FV = p^{2d} on the whole complex (next page) mixes degrees and is only meaningful after passing to isocrystals, as he himself notes.

An 'absolute' crystalline site of S over Spec Z with nilpotent PD-thickenings, giving a Frobenius for every p at once, is not what Berthelot later built (he works over a fixed PD base, typically Z_p or W(k)). Making 'DR(f)_p' and the F_p glue globally over Z is left vague. Perfectness over the absolute site in mixed/zero characteristic was not addressed.

ideas.what: Derived category of crystals; pseudo-coherent/perfect complexes of crystals defined by evaluation on all thickenings
ideas.modern_name: Perfect crystalline complexes / quasi-coherent derived crystals (D_qc of the crystalline or de Rham stack)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966–68), Berthelot (1974), Berthelot–Ogus; ∞-categorical version Bhatt–Lurie, Drinfeld
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968); this letter to Tate is widely cited

ideas.what: Crystalline de Rham cohomology DR(f) of a smooth proper f as a perfect complex of crystals, base-change compatible, with Künneth, Poincaré duality and comparison DR(f)(S) ≅ Rf_*Ω_{X/S}
ideas.modern_name: Relative crystalline cohomology Rf_{cris*}O_{X/S}; Berthelot's base change, Künneth and duality theorems; Berthelot–Ogus comparison
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés (Crystals and de Rham cohomology); letter to Tate 1966

ideas.what: Tate crystal T^d as dualising object for crystalline Poincaré duality
ideas.modern_name: Unit F-crystal twisted by p^d (Tate twist O(-d)) in crystalline duality

ideas.what: Frobenius F_p on DR(f) restricted mod p via relative Frobenius and base change, for every prime p simultaneously, making DR(f) a 'bi-isocrystal'
ideas.modern_name: F-crystal / F-isocrystal structure on crystalline cohomology; Frobenius at all primes ~ Λ-structures / prismatic (absolute) cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, Berthelot, Mazur (F-crystals); global-over-Z versions loosely Borger, Bhatt–Scholze
ideas.where_published: Letter to Tate (circulated); Dix exposés discusses Frobenius on crystals

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks for a single absolute crystalline object over S/Z carrying a Frobenius F_p for every prime p at once, with de Rham cohomology as its value on S. This is close in spirit to later global-over-Z frameworks: absolute prismatic or de Rham–Witt-type cohomology, and Borger's Λ-algebraic geometry, i.e. Frobenius lifts at all primes. The letter is, however, already known and cited, so this is a retrospective resonance rather than an uncredited result.
missed.quote: on trouve pour chaque entier p un homomorphisme de frobenius F_p : DR(f)_p^{(p)} -> DR(f)_p
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: an early formulation of 'cohomology over Z with all Frobenii' that predates Λ-ring and prismatic approaches. It is a minor point for historians of p-adic Hodge theory.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known 1966 Grothendieck–Tate letter that launched crystalline cohomology. Its programme (perfectness, base change, Künneth, duality, comparison with de Rham, Frobenius) was realised by Berthelot and is credited to Grothendieck. Only the 'absolute over Z, all p at once' bi-isocrystal framing is slightly unusual.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'logène C de S' — the handwritten 'C' is the name of the crystalline site, inserted after 'cristallogène'.
'complexe de cristaux (absolu) DR(f) sur S' — 'absolu' and 'sur S' are handwritten insertions; 'cristalline' is inserted above 'De Rham'.
'2.3. La cohomologie de De Rham comme bi-isocristal' — 'iso' handwritten above 'bicristal'.
Tate crystal weight: typed 'd' corrected by hand to '2d'; the '[2d]' brackets are handwritten.
